name: CSS Specificity Calculator
blurb: which of two selectors wins, and why
intro: Counts IDs, classes and types for two selectors, including :is(), :not(), :has(), :where() and :nth-child(… of S), and says which one wins, by !important, specificity or source order. Counting follows Selectors Level 4; the order of checks follows CSS Cascading Level 5.

inputs.label: B comes later in the stylesheet

usage: Give two selectors as text (a pasted rule 'sel { … }' is fine), whether each declaration is !important, and whether B comes later in the stylesheet. It returns each specificity as (IDs, classes, types), the winner and the reason (importance, specificity column, or source order), and a per-part breakdown. Use it to explain why a style does not apply or to choose a selector that overrides another.
sources: W3C Selectors Level 4, section 17 'Calculating a selector's specificity'
W3C CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5, section 6 'Cascading' (importance, layers, specificity, order of appearance)
